title: Three names
intro: Üç kişi kendini tanıtıyor. Herkes adını, nereli olduğunu ve nerede yaşadığını söylüyor.
text:
Hello! My name is Deniz. I am from Turkey. I live in Izmir. Izmir is a big city. I am a student. I am not married.

Hello! My name is Ana. I am from Spain. I live in a town in the north. I am a teacher. I am very happy here.

Hello! My name is Tom. I am from Ireland. I am not from Turkey, but I live in Turkey now. My city is Izmir too. Deniz and I meet on Friday.

questions.text: Where is Deniz from?
questions.explain: „I am from Turkey.“ — Deniz Türkiye'den. Spain Ana'nın, Ireland Tom'un ülkesi.

questions.text: Who is a teacher?
questions.explain: „I am a teacher.“ satırı Ana'nın paragrafında. Deniz öğrenci, Tom ne olduğunu söylemiyor.

questions.text: Deniz is married.
questions.explain: „I am not married.“ — „not“ cümleyi olumsuz yapıyor, yani evli değil.

questions.text: Ana lives in a town in the ___.
questions.explain: „I live in a town in the north.“ — kuzeyde bir kasabada.

questions.text: Where does Tom live now?
questions.explain: „I am not from Turkey, but I live in Turkey now.“ — Tom İrlandalı ama Türkiye'de yaşıyor.

title: Are you a student here?
intro: Mert ile Lena ilk kez tanışıyor. Kısa bir selamlaşma, tanışma ve hal hatır sorma.
text:
Mert: Hello! Excuse me, are you a student here?
Lena: Hi! Yes, I am. My name is Lena.
Mert: I am Mert. Where are you from, Lena?
Lena: I am from Germany. I live in Bremen. And you?
Mert: I am from Turkey. I live in this town now.
Lena: How are you today?
Mert: I am fine, thanks. But I am very hungry! And you?
Lena: I am not hungry, I am thirsty. And I am a little tired.
Mert: Are you a teacher too?
Lena: No, I am not a teacher. I am a student.
Mert: Good! See you on Monday. Goodbye!
Lena: Goodbye, Mert!

questions.explain: „I am from Germany. I live in Bremen.“ — ülke Almanya, şehir Bremen.

questions.text: How is Mert today?
questions.explain: „I am fine, thanks. But I am very hungry!“ — yorgun ve susamış olan Lena.

questions.text: Lena is a teacher.
questions.explain: „No, I am not a teacher. I am a student.“ — öğretmen değil, öğrenci.

questions.text: Lena lives in ___.
questions.explain: „I live in Bremen.“ — Almanya ülkesi, Bremen şehri; boşluğa şehir giriyor.

questions.text: Konuşmanın sırası: doğru sıraya koy.
questions.explain: Önce soru, sonra ad, sonra „nerelisin“, sonra ülke. Tanışma hep bu sırayla gidiyor.

questions.text: Is Mert from Turkey?
questions.explain: „I am from Turkey.“ — evet. Kısa cevap „Yes, he is.“ biçiminde kurulur.

title: English course — A1
intro: Bir dil okulunun kurs ilanını oku: ne zaman başlıyor, kim veriyor, ne kadar tutuyor.
text:
ENGLISH COURSE — A1

Do you speak a little English? Come and learn with us.

The course is easy. We start on Monday, September 7. One lesson is ninety minutes. We write words, we say words, and we spell our names.

Your teacher is Nora Scott. She is from Ireland. She is a very good teacher.

Price: forty euros for one month. For students: thirty euros. How much is a pen? One euro.

Do you understand every word? No — and that is not a problem. We say it again.

questions.explain: „We start on Monday, September 7.“ — bir ay fiyatın süresi, başlangıç günü değil.

questions.explain: „Your teacher is Nora Scott. She is from Ireland.“

questions.text: The course is forty euros for students.
questions.explain: Öğrenciler için otuz euro: „For students: thirty euros.“ Kırk euro ötekiler için.

questions.text: One lesson is ___ minutes.
questions.explain: „One lesson is ninety minutes.“ Sayıyı yazıyla da rakamla da yazabilirsin.

questions.text: How much is a pen?
questions.explain: „How much is a pen? One euro.“ — fiyatta „years old“ gibi bir ek yok, sayı tek başına duruyor.

title: What do you do?
intro: İki kişi işlerini, yaşlarını ve konuştukları dilleri anlatıyor.
text:
Ana: Hello! I am Ana. What do you do?
Sam: Hi, Ana. I am a doctor. I work in a big hospital. And you?
Ana: I am a singer. I work in a school too — I am a music teacher there.
Sam: Very good! Do you speak English?
Ana: Yes, I do. I speak a little English and a little German.
Sam: How do you spell your name?
Ana: A, N, A. It is easy!
Sam: And how old are you, Ana?
Ana: I am twenty-nine years old. And you?
Sam: I am forty. My job is not easy, but I am happy.
Ana: Can you say that again, please? You speak very fast!
Sam: I said: I am happy.

questions.explain: „A, N, A. It is easy!“ — harfleme harfleri tek tek söylemektir.

title: This is my family
intro: Ayla ailesini anlatıyor. Okurken kimin kim olduğunu ve yaşları takip et.
text:
Hello! My name is Ayla. This is my family.

My mother is a doctor. Her name is Sevgi. She is fifty-two years old. My father is a teacher. His name is Kemal.

I have got one sister and one brother. My sister is twenty and my brother is only nine. He is still a boy, but he grows very fast!

My grandma and my grandpa live in a small town. Their house is old. We are there in May, for my grandma's birthday. We eat cake and we are all very happy.

title: Our animals
intro: Bir aile evcil hayvanlarını anlatıyor. Kimin hangi hayvanı var, hangisi ne yapmıyor?
text:
Hello! This is a photo of my family and our animals.

I have a dog. Its name is Luna. Luna is very big and she is not young. She plays with my brother. My sister has two cats. Their names are Mia and Nil. The cats don't play with Luna — they only sleep.

We have a bird too. Its name is Pit. Pit doesn't talk, and he never sings. My father says: "Don't forget the bird!"

We don't have a horse. A horse is for a farm, not for a house. But there are many horses at the zoo.

questions.explain: „I have a dog. Its name is Luna.“ — Mia kedilerden biri, Pit kuş.

questions.text: Who has two cats?

questions.explain: „But there are many horses at the zoo.“ — evde at yok, hayvanat bahçesinde var.

title: Who is this?
intro: Eda bir fotoğrafı anlatıyor. „this“, „that“ ve „these“ arasındaki farka dikkat et.
text:
Ali: This is a good photo. Who is this?
Eda: This is my mother. And these are my friends.
Ali: How many people are there in the photo?
Eda: There are many people — one, two, three … eight!
Ali: Is that a man or a woman?
Eda: That is a man. He doesn't live here. He is from Ankara.
Ali: And this group here?
Eda: Those are my cousins. I don't know all their names!
Ali: You have a big family.
Eda: Yes. But I don't have a brother. I only have two sisters.
Ali: Is there an animal in the photo?
Eda: Yes, there is a dog. Its name is Nero. Don't forget Nero!

questions.explain: „one, two, three … eight!“ — Eda sayıyor ve sekizde bitiriyor.

questions.explain: „there is a dog. Its name is Nero.“ — hayvan için „its“ kullanılıyor.

title: My friend Kaan
intro: Bir arkadaş anlatılıyor: hem nasıl göründüğü hem nasıl biri olduğu.
text:
My friend Kaan is nineteen. He is very tall and he has got short hair. His eyes are green.

Kaan is not quiet. He is funny, and he talks a lot. He is kind too — he never forgets a birthday.

We work together in a small school. After work we play a game or we talk about music. Kaan likes music very much.

Kaan's cousin Ada is in our club. She is quiet, but she is nice. Her hair is long and she looks like Kaan. They are a funny group!

title: What does he look like?
intro: Sena akrabalarını anlatıyor. „look like“ görünüşü sorar — cevabı da görünüş olmalı.
text:
Mert: Who is that man? Is he your uncle?
Sena: No, he isn't. That is my grandfather.
Mert: Really? He looks very strong!
Sena: Yes, he is. He is seventy-one, but he plays with us every day.
Mert: And the woman with him?
Sena: That is my grandmother. My grandparents live together in Izmir.
Mert: What does your aunt look like?
Sena: She is short and she has got long hair. She is very funny.
Mert: Is she busy?
Sena: Yes, she is always busy. She has got four children.
Mert: Four! Ali's cousin has got four children too.
Sena: I know. Ada is my friend.

title: The food I love
intro: Biri sevdiği ve sevmediği yemekleri anlatıyor. Kim neyi tercih ediyor?
text:
I love food. I cook every day, and I like eating with my family.

The food I love most is pizza with meat and onion. I don't like sweet food — I hate very sweet cakes! My sister prefers rice. She says rice is cheap and easy.

At the market I buy meat, onions and rice. The meat is expensive: nine euros a kilo. In a sale it is cheaper.

I prefer tea to coffee. In the morning I drink a big cup of tea with milk. My father drinks only water. He says: "Don't cook with wine!"

title: At the market
intro: Pazarda pazarlık. Kilo, gram ve fiyat art arda geliyor — sayıları takip et.

Seller: Good morning! How many kilos do you want?
Ayla: Two kilos of tomatoes, please. Are they fresh?
Seller: Very fresh. They are from a farm near the city.
Ayla: How much is it?
Seller: Four euros. Tomatoes are cheap this week — it's a sale.
Ayla: Good. And the meat? I'd like five hundred grams.
Seller: The meat is eighteen euros a kilo, so nine euros.
Ayla: Nine euros! That's too expensive for me.
Seller: Then take three hundred grams. It costs five euros.
Ayla: Yes, please. And a bottle of water too.
Seller: Here you are. Eleven euros, please.
Ayla: Thank you. Can I pay with coins?
Seller: Of course!

title: My day
intro: Bir günün tamamı saatleriyle anlatılıyor. Hangi iş hangi saatte?
text:
I wake up at six and I get up at a quarter past six. I take a shower and then I have breakfast: bread, cheese and a cup of tea.

I work from eight until five. At lunchtime I eat a sandwich with tomatoes and carrots. I don't work on Sunday.

After work I buy fruit and vegetables at the market: apples, potatoes and bananas. A kilo of apples costs two euros.

I have dinner at half past seven. At midnight I sleep. I am always tired at night!

title: My week
intro: Bir haftanın düzeni. Hangi iş her zaman, hangisi bazen yapılıyor?
text:
I always get up at seven, also at the weekend. First I wake up, then I put on my clothes and I turn on the radio.

On Monday and on Friday I work in the city. I usually walk to work. Sometimes I am late, but my teacher is never angry.

In the evening I turn off the radio and I sit down with a newspaper. I often sit there until midnight.

At the weekend I look for a good game. After that I cook. Finally, before I sleep, I drink a cup of warm milk. That is my usual day.

title: Come in, sit down
intro: Geç kalan bir öğrenci. Phrasal verb'lerin hepsi bir arada: come in, sit down, turn on, look for.
text:
Teacher: Good morning! Come in and sit down, please.
Ali: Good morning. Sorry, I am late again.
Teacher: It's only a quarter past nine. What time do you get up?
Ali: I usually wake up at seven, but today my clock doesn't work.
Teacher: Turn on your phone at night, then.
Ali: I always turn it off before I sleep.
Teacher: Then look for a new clock at the weekend!
Ali: Yes. On Saturday I have time.
Teacher: Good. Now, first take off your bag and sit down.
Ali: Sorry again!
Teacher: Never mind. We begin at half past nine. You are not late.

title: A work day
intro: Bir iş günü baştan sona. İş kaçta başlıyor, kaçta bitiyor, sonrası ne oluyor?
text:
I work in a big office in the city. The building is old but it is very nice.

I start work at eight and I finish at five. At lunch I eat with my friends in the café near the office. In the afternoon I usually have a meeting.

I have a meeting on Friday with a new group. I am not going to be late!

After work I am free. I like reading, and I don't like listening to the radio. In the evening I watch a film on television. Sometimes I walk by the sea.

title: What time do you open?

text:
Ela: Good morning. What time do you open?
Shop: We open at nine and we close at seven.
Ela: And on Sunday?
Shop: On Sunday we are closed.
Ela: Is the office in the same building?
Shop: Yes, it is. The office opens early, at eight.
Ela: I'd like to come tomorrow. Is that a problem?
Shop: No. Tomorrow is Friday, we are open all day.
Ela: When does the bus leave from the city?
Shop: Every hour. The next bus leaves at ten.
Ela: Then I am going to take the bus at ten. Is my card ready?
Shop: Yes, your card is ready. Don't be late — we close at seven!

title: A gift for my mother
intro: Doğum günü hediyesi seçiliyor. Hangi fikir neden eleniyor?
text:
Tomorrow is my mother's birthday. I want to buy a gift for her, but I don't have many ideas.

A ring is beautiful, but it is very expensive. Chocolate is cheap, but it is not special. My sister says: "Buy a red sweater. She likes red."

I think that is a good idea. I am going to the store in the afternoon. I don't have much time — the store closes at six.

My sister is going to come with me. She always chooses perfect gifts. "What do you think?" I am going to ask her a lot!

title: Places to visit
intro: Şehir rehberi. Ne zaman açık, nereye nasıl gidiliyor?
text:
WELCOME TO OUR CITY

You can visit the museum every day from ten to six. The museum of art is near the park, behind the old church.

Can I see the park? Of course — the park is open at all hours and it is free. You can go on foot or by bike.

The church is open today, but not on Monday. Photography is not a problem, but please be quiet.

At the information desk you can ask for a map. A visitor can also take a boat on the river. The boat starts every hour.

intro: Bir daire tanıtılıyor. Hangi oda nerede, içinde ne var?
text:
This is my home. It is an apartment on the second floor, with three rooms.

There is a big living room with a sofa and a lamp. The kitchen is small, but there is a fridge and a table with four chairs. There are two bedrooms. In my bedroom there is a bed under the window.

Is there a bathroom? Yes, there is one next to the kitchen. The toilet is in the bathroom.

We also have a cellar downstairs. The stairs are old, so please be quiet on them. My neighbour is very friendly, but she works at night.

Ela: Where is my phone? I don't find it.

Ela: No, only a book and a lamp are on the table.
Can: Under the sofa?
Ela: No. And not under the bed.
Can: In the kitchen? Next to the fridge?
Ela: I look. No, it is not there. Is there a phone in the bathroom?
Can: Why a phone in the bathroom? But look, please.

title: House rules
intro: Apartman kuralları. Ne yasak, ne serbest, ne zaman?
text:
HOUSE RULES

You must be quiet from ten at night to seven in the morning. You mustn't make noise on Sunday.

The stairs must be clean. Please put the rubbish in the bin downstairs, not in front of your door.

Is it allowed to have a party? Yes, but you have to ask your neighbours. A party has to end at eleven.

Water and electricity are not included in the rent. Each apartment pays the bill every month.

In a fire: don't take the lift. Go down the stairs.

Thank you!

text:
In the summer I go to the pool every week. I can swim, but not very fast.

The water is cold in the morning and warm in the afternoon. I take a towel and my earphones — I listen to music in the water.

title: Parts of the body
intro: Vücut bölümleri ve ağrının iki söyleniş biçimi.
text:
This is my body. This is my head, and these are my ears. My hands have five fingers each.

Is this your arm? Yes, and this is my shoulder. The leg is long and the knee is in the middle of it.

Where is the heart? On the left side, in the body. The blood goes from the heart to every finger.

When something hurts, we say: "My head hurts" or "I have a headache." Both are good English. If you feel very bad, you must go to a doctor.

title: Healthy living
intro: Sağlıklı yaşam öğütleri. Ne yapmalı, ne yapmamalı?
text:
Do you want to be healthy? It is simple.

You should eat fruit every day: an apple, a banana, a carrot. A salad with chicken is good for dinner too.

You shouldn't smoke. And you shouldn't eat a big dinner at ten in the evening.

Should I do exercise? Yes! Twenty minutes a day is good. You can walk, run or swim — all three are exercise.

Is weight a problem? Then you should drink more water and eat less sugar. But be careful: a fast change is not healthy. Slow is better.

title: At the dentist
intro: Diş hekiminde. Ne zaman ağrıyor, sebebi ne?
text:
Dentist: Good morning. Please sit here. What is the problem?
Kaan: I have a toothache. My tooth hurts since two days.
Dentist: Which tooth? This one?
Kaan: Yes! That one.
Dentist: Does it hurt with cold water?
Kaan: Very much. And with ice cream too. And with lemon.
Dentist: I see. The tooth is not clean here. Do you eat a lot of sugar?
Kaan: Maybe. I eat ice cream every evening.
Dentist: Then you should eat less ice cream. And you should come every year.
Kaan: I know. I am here after four years.
Dentist: Four years! Today I clean the tooth. Come again in one week.
Kaan: Does it hurt today?
Dentist: A little. But after that you feel better.

intro: Postanede mektup ve paket. Hangi fiyat neye ait?

Clerk: Of course. What is in it? Only paper?
Ela: Only paper and a photo.
Clerk: Then it is two euros.
Ela: And how much is a stamp for Germany?
Clerk: One euro.
Ela: I have a parcel too. How much is that?
Clerk: The parcel is heavy. Nine euros. Is it full?
Ela: Yes, full. Books and a plastic box.
Ela: Can I have two stamps, please? For two letters tomorrow.
Clerk: Here you are. And here is a pencil — you have to write the address.
Ela: The address of the parcel is on the paper.
Clerk: Good. Twelve euros together, please.
Ela: Here is my card. Thank you!

title: My last weekend
intro: Geçen hafta sonu anlatılıyor. Düzensiz geçmiş biçimlerini yakala.
text:
What did you do last weekend? I went to the mountains with two friends.

We went by train on Saturday morning. The weather was sunny. We walked four hours and we saw a river and a small farm.

In the evening we ate in a café near the lake. I had soup and bread, my friend had chicken.

On Sunday I visited my grandmother. She was very happy. We watched a film and I finished my homework there.

I didn't watch TV in the evening — I was too tired. I went to bed at nine!

title: I lost my phone
intro: Kaybolan bir telefonun hikâyesi. Ne zaman ne oldu, sırasıyla takip et.
text:
Last week I lost my phone on the bus. It was a bad day.

I was waiting for the bus in the rain. When the bus came, I was holding my bag in one hand and my phone in the other. I got in, I sat down and I fell asleep.

Two stops later I woke up suddenly and I ran out. The phone was on the seat.

I went back to the bus station the day before yesterday. A woman there was very kind. "Somebody brought a phone yesterday," she said. And it was my phone!

I bought a small bag for the phone. Now I always put it in the bag. I don't want to lose it again.

title: What were you doing?
intro: İki kişi dün ne yaptıklarını konuşuyor. Hangi iş sürüyordu, hangisi bir andı?
text:
Ali: What were you doing yesterday at eight? I called you three times.
Sena: At eight? I was cooking. My phone was in the other room.
Ali: I called again at nine.
Sena: At nine I was sleeping! I went to bed early.
Ali: Early? Why?
Sena: Because I worked twelve hours. While I was working, it was raining all day.
Ali: And this morning?
Sena: This morning I was waiting for the bus when I saw your message.
Ali: Good. I lost my keys last week and I found them yesterday — in your car!
Sena: In my car! When did you leave them there?
Ali: Two weeks ago, I think. I was wearing a big jacket that day and the keys fell down.
Sena: Then come and take them. I am at home now.

title: My childhood
intro: Bir çocukluk anlatısı. Eskiden ne vardı, sonra ne değişti?
text:
I grew up in a small village near the sea. When I was a child, we didn't have a computer and I didn't use to watch television.

First I went to kindergarten in the village, then to the primary school in the next town. Every morning we walked twenty minutes, and in the winter it was very cold.

I used to play football in the yard with the children of our neighbours. My sister used to play with her doll and she used to shout at us because we were loud.

After that, when I was ten, we moved to the city. At first I didn't like it. The new school was big and I didn't know anybody.

But I remember one good thing: the city had a library. I used to read there every afternoon.

title: A holiday I remember
intro: Bir tatil anlatısı. Sıralama sözcüklerini takip et: first, then, after that, finally.
text:
I went to Antalya last summer with two friends. It was my first flight.

First we took a taxi to the airport. Then we waited two hours because the plane was late. At first I was angry, but afterwards it was fine.

We stayed at a small hotel for five days. The weather was hot and the beach was beautiful. Every morning we swam in the sea, and after that we ate fruit in the shade.

One day we took a boat to an island. While we were on the boat, a big fish jumped out of the water. My friend was wearing a white shirt and the water made it wet. That's why we have a funny photo of that day.

I enjoyed the holiday very much. Next year I want to go again.

title: What happened?
intro: Küçük bir kaza anlatılıyor. Ne oldu, ne kadar ciddi, sonrası ne?
text:
Sena: What happened to your arm?
Ali: I fell on the stairs yesterday and I hurt my arm. Luckily, it wasn't serious.
Sena: Where did it happen?
Ali: At home. I was carrying two boxes and I didn't see the last step.
Sena: Were you alone?
Ali: Yes, I was alone. But my neighbour heard me and she came fast.
Sena: Did you go to the doctor?
Ali: Yes. I waited two hours there. The doctor said: No break, only a bad injury.
Sena: How long do you have to wait?
Ali: Two weeks with no heavy work. Bad luck — we are moving to a new flat next month!
Sena: Then I help you. I have moved four times in my life.
Ali: Really? Thank you very much.

Nil: Have you ever been abroad?
Kaan: Yes, I have. I have been to Italy twice.
Nil: Twice! When was the first time?
Kaan: Three years ago. I went with my sister and we stayed in a hostel.
Nil: Have you ever tried Italian food there?
Kaan: Of course. Every day! It was exciting.
Nil: I have never been abroad. But my brother has gone to London — he is away this week.
Kaan: Is he coming back soon?
Nil: Yes, he comes back on Sunday. He goes there once a year for his work.
Kaan: Then ask him about foreign countries. He knows a lot.
Nil: I will. Have you ever been to England?
Kaan: No, I haven't. But I want to go.

title: My life story
intro: Bir hayat hikâyesi. „since“ ve „for“ art arda geçiyor — hangisi süre, hangisi başlangıç?
text:
I was born in a small town in the north. My parents worked in a factory and we lived there for eleven years.

Then I moved to the city because I wanted to study. I have lived here since two thousand and fifteen — that is ten years.

At the university I met my wife. We have known each other for nine years now. Our marriage was in May, and since then my life has changed a lot.

I have already finished my studies, but I haven't found a good job yet. I work in a café at the moment. It is not bad: the people are friendly and the hours are on time.

Next year I'm going to look for work abroad. I promise I won't stay in the café for years!

title: Have you finished yet?
intro: İşte bir rapor bekleniyor. „already“, „yet“ ve „just“ üçü de geçiyor.
text:
Boss: Have you finished the report yet?
Ela: Almost. I have already written four pages, but I haven't finished the last part yet.
Boss: How long have you been at it?
Ela: Since nine this morning. For five hours!
Boss: And the numbers? Are they ready?
Ela: I have just sent them to Deniz. He is going to read them.
Boss: Good. The meeting is at four, so we have two hours.
Ela: Don't worry, it will be ready on time. I promise.
Boss: I know. You have worked here for three years and you have never been late.
Ela: Thank you. But I'm going to take a break now — ten minutes.
Boss: Of course. Take twenty.
Ela: Then the report will be complete at half past three.

title: Me, then and now
intro: On yıl önce ve şimdi. Ne değişti, ne aynı kaldı?
text:
Ten years ago my life was very different. I used to work in a big office in the city. The job was important but difficult, and I was tired every evening.

Now I work at home. The money is less, but the hours are better and I am still here at six when my children come back from school.

I used to travel a lot. I don't travel anymore — or almost not. Last year I was abroad only once.

Some things are the same. I still read every night, and my favourite café is still the little one near the park. It is tiny, but the coffee is excellent and it is cheaper than the big places in the centre.

My dream is to write a book. That is my goal for the next two years.

title: The best day
intro: Hayatın en güzel günü anlatılıyor. Üstünlük biçimlerini yakala.
text:
The best day of my life was in June two years ago. It was not a big day for other people, but for me it was excellent.

I had an opportunity: a company abroad wanted me for a new job. The letter came in the morning. I read it three times.

The job was more important than my old one, and the money was better too. But the best thing was not the money. The best thing was this: somebody read my work and said yes.

I called my mother and she cried. Then I called my sister — she is the most practical person in our family — and she asked: "Is the flat cheaper there or more expensive?"

It's the best memory I have ever had. And yes, the flat was more expensive.

title: Describing symptoms
intro: Hekimde şikâyet anlatılıyor. Ne kadar zamandır, ne kadar ciddi?
text:
Doctor: Good morning. What is the problem?
Ela: I have a fever and my throat is sore. I've had a cough for three days.
Doctor: How long have you had the fever?
Ela: Since Monday. It started in the evening.
Doctor: And is it worse now or better?
Ela: Worse. Yesterday I was dizzy in the morning and I couldn't work.
Doctor: Do you have a pain in the stomach?
Ela: No, only the throat and the head.
Doctor: It is a cold, not a serious illness. You should rest for a week.
Ela: A week! I have a lot of work.
Doctor: Then you will be ill for a month. You should drink enough water, avoid cold drinks and relax.
Ela: Should I take vitamins?
Doctor: They don't hurt. But rest is the best medicine.

title: Changing an appointment
intro: Randevu değiştiriliyor. Hangi gün kalıyor, hangisi iptal?
text:
Deniz: Good morning. I'd like to change my appointment.
Office: Of course. What is your name?
Deniz: Deniz Kaya. The appointment is on Friday at ten.
Office: I see it. When would you like to come?
Deniz: Do you have anything earlier? Friday is too late for me.
Office: Let me look. Wednesday at two is available. Or Thursday at half past eight.
Deniz: Thursday is better. Half past eight is fine.
Office: Good. And Friday? Do I cancel it?
Deniz: Yes, please cancel it.
Office: Is the problem urgent?
Deniz: Not urgent, but I have had the pain for two weeks and it is getting worse.
Office: Then Thursday is good. If it is worse tomorrow, call back and we find something today.
Deniz: Thank you. I'll let you know.

title: At the pharmacy
intro: Kutunun üstündeki talimat konuşuluyor. Kaç tane, ne zaman, yan etkisi ne?
text:
Pharmacist: Good morning. How can I help you?
Ela: I have this from my doctor. It is my first time with this medicine.
Pharmacist: Let me look. One tablet twice a day.
Ela: Twice a day — in the morning and in the evening?
Pharmacist: Yes. And you should take it after meals, never before.
Ela: Why after a meal?
Pharmacist: Because of the stomach. On an empty stomach it can hurt.
Ela: How many tablets are in the box?
Pharmacist: Twenty. That is ten days.
Ela: Are there side effects?
Pharmacist: You can get tired. Don't drive in the first two days.
Ela: My son has the same cold. Can he take it too?
Pharmacist: No. For children we have a syrup. This dose is for adults.
Ela: Good to know. And if I forget a pill?
Pharmacist: Take the next one at the normal time. Never take two together.

title: A morning at the hospital
intro: Bir sabah, üç masa: danışma, servis, sigorta. Ne gerekiyordu?
text:
On Monday my father had an appointment at the hospital. We were there at eight.
First we went to the information desk. The nurse asked for his card and his documents.
Then we had to wait in line for the ward. Ten people were before us and we waited an hour.
The doctor looked at the results from March and said the treatment was working well.
After that we went to the insurance office. A woman gave us a form and asked for a signature.
My father asked: Does my insurance cover this? She said yes, but he has to pay ten euros for the medicine.
Then a nurse showed us the hospital room for Friday. It is a small room with two beds.
On the way home my father said: The waiting was long, but everybody was kind.
Now I know one thing: take the card, the documents and a book.

title: Are you OK?
intro: Mülakat öncesi. Kim neyden endişeli, kim neyden korkuyor?

Nil: Are you OK? You look worried.
Can: I am. I have a job interview on Thursday and I'm afraid of the questions.
Nil: Which questions?
Can: The last time they asked me about my old job and I said nothing good. I was so stressed.
Nil: And what happened?
Can: They said no. I was disappointed for a week.
Nil: This time you are better. You know the company and you have more experience.
Can: Maybe. But I'm worried about the money question. What do I say?
Nil: Say a number, not a story. And breathe before you answer.
Can: You are always so relaxed. How do you do it?
Nil: I am not relaxed. I only look relaxed. That is half of the work.
Can: Then I will learn that too.

title: Four flats in two weeks
intro: Dört daire, dört kusur. Sonunda seçilen en güzeli değil.
text:
We looked at four flats in two weeks. The first one was cheap, but it was on the ground floor and very dark.
The second had a beautiful balcony, but the rent was eight hundred euros. Too much for us.
The third one was in an old building. The rooms were spacious and bright, the ceiling was high.
But the advert said „furnished“ and there was only a bed and a table.
The fourth flat was small. The rooms were normal and the kitchen was old.
But it was quiet, the neighbours were friendly and the deposit was only one month.
We took the fourth. My sister asked: Why the small one?
I said: Because I sleep there. In the first one I would never sleep — the street is under the window.
We have been here since March and I am happy. The flat is smaller than my old one, but my life is bigger.

title: Telling the landlord
intro: İki arıza bildiriliyor. Hangisi ne zamandan beri sürüyor?
text:
Dear Mr Yılmaz,
I am writing about two problems in my flat.
There's a leak in the bathroom. The water comes from the pipe under the sink and it has been there since Saturday. There is already damage on the carpet.
The second problem is the heating. The heating hasn't worked since Monday. In the morning the rooms are very cold and my daughter is ill.
I called the caretaker twice. He came on Tuesday, looked at the pipe and said: I can't fix it.
Could you send someone today or tomorrow? I am at home after four.
If it is easier for you, I can be at home on Saturday too.
Thank you very much.
Best wishes,
Ela Demir

title: Moving in
intro: Taşınma günü, adım adım. Ne bitti, ne henüz bitmedi?
text:
We moved in on the first of March. First, we signed the contract in the office of the old building.
After that, we got the keys — three for the front door and one for the flat.
The furniture came at eleven. Two men carried the cupboard up the stairs and it didn't go through the door.
In the end they took the drawers out and then it was fine.
The first night we slept on the carpet, because the bed was still in the hallway.
There is a big mirror in the corner of the bedroom. It was already here before us.
We haven't turned on the electricity yet, so we ate bread and cheese with a light from the phone.
The gas man comes on Thursday. Until then, cold water.
My brother asked: Was it a good day? I said: The best. Nothing was ready, but everything was ours.

segments.text: The family above us moved in in June. Since then, Saturday night is not my night.

segments.speaker: Nil

Ela: Hello, is that the repair service?
Mechanic: Yes. What is the problem?
Ela: My washing machine isn't working. It starts and then it stops after two minutes.
Mechanic: Since when?
Ela: Since Friday. The caretaker looked at it but he had no tools.
Mechanic: I see. Can you tell me the name on the machine?
Ela: It says Bosch, and under it a number.
Mechanic: Good. Can I come tomorrow morning?
Ela: Tomorrow is difficult. I work until four.
Mechanic: Then Thursday at five.
Ela: That is fine. How much will it cost?
Mechanic: The visit is thirty euros. With a new part it can be a hundred.
Ela: Could you give me an estimate first?
Mechanic: Of course. I look at it, I tell you the price, and then you decide.

Rules for the residents
You have to put the rubbish in the garbage can before eight in the evening. The caretaker takes it out on Monday and Thursday.
You mustn't make noise between ten at night and seven in the morning. On Sunday the quiet time is all day.
You don't have to clean the stairs. A company comes every week. But you have to clean the balcony in front of your flat.
Bikes are forbidden in the hallway. There is a room for them next to the front door.
The attic is open from April to October. From November it is closed, because the roof is old.
If something is broken, tell the caretaker or write to the landlord. Please don't repair it.
Thank you — a quiet building is a good building.

text:
Dear Mr Arda,
I am writing about the kitchen helper position in your advert.
I have worked in a kitchen for four years. From 2021 to 2023 I worked at a big company with a canteen for three hundred people. After that I worked for two years in a small restaurant near the station.
In the canteen I learned to work fast and in a team. In the small restaurant I learned everything else: the long evenings, the money and the noise.
I have also worked with a cook from Italy, so I know a little Italian, but my English is better.
I can start on the first of March. I am free every day and I have already talked to my old boss.
Thank you for reading this. I hope to hear from you.
Best wishes,
Deniz Kaya

title: What I do at work
intro: Sıradan bir salı. Hangi iş ne kadar sürüyor?
text:
People ask me what I do all day. Here is a normal Tuesday.
I usually answer emails in the morning, from nine to half past ten. Most of them are from customers with the same three questions.
Then I check the numbers from Monday. If something is wrong, I call the department downstairs. That happens twice a week.
At twelve we eat. At one the regular meeting starts — twenty minutes, never more.
In the afternoon I write reports. I write two reports a week, one short and one long. The long one takes three hours and nobody reads it. I know that, my boss knows that, and we both say nothing.
The last task of the day is the list for tomorrow. Five things, in order. If I don't write it, I sleep badly.
That is the whole job. It looks boring here. It isn't.

Dear Ms Kaya,
Could I take a day off on Friday? My sister arrives from Ankara in the morning and I would like to meet her at the station.
I have already talked to Mert and he can do my tasks that day. The reports for the week are finished and the meeting on Friday is not mine.
If Friday is not possible, would it be possible to leave early, at two? Then I can work in the morning and still meet her.
I have one more question. I have five vacation days this year. Can I take three of them in August? I ask now because my brother arranges his holiday in May.
Thank you very much. If you need anything from me before Friday, tell me today or tomorrow.
Best wishes,
Nil

title: Online orders
intro: Kayıp paket için forum. Önce ne yapmalı?
text:
Question: I ordered a chair two weeks ago and it hasn't arrived yet. What can I do?
Answer 1: First track the package. In your account there is a number. With that number you see where it is. Usually it stands in a city two hours away and comes on Monday.
Answer 2: I had the same problem in March. The package was at my neighbour's door for six days. Nobody wrote to me. Ask the people in your building first.
Answer 3: Write to the shop, not to the driver. The shop has the contract with you. Write short: the order number, the date and one question — when will it arrive?
Answer 4: And put everything in one email. I sent four emails in two days and they answered the first one after a week.
Question: Thank you. It arrived this morning. It was in the wrong building for ten days. Nobody understands it.

Post: Normal or express? Express is faster, but it's more expensive.
Ela: How much more is express?
Post: Normal is eleven euros and takes six days. Express is twenty-four and takes two days.
Ela: And is it safe? There are books inside and one of them is old.
Post: Then insure it. For three euros more the post pays if something happens.
Ela: Good. Normal with insurance, please.
Post: Fill in this form. Name, street, zip code and what is inside.
Ela: Do I write the price of the books?
Post: Yes. Not the price in the shop — what they cost you.
Ela: Fourteen euros for six days. Cheaper than I expected.

title: At the airport
intro: Havaalanı yönergesi. Ne zorunlu, nerede bakılır?
text:
Before the gate
Put your bag on the belt. Big luggage goes at the desk, small bags go with you. Water is not allowed after this point — drink it or leave it here.
At the gate you have to show your boarding pass and your passport. Both. Every time.
Boarding starts forty minutes before the flight. If there is a delay, you see it on the screen in the terminal, not on your phone. The screen is always first.
In the plane: bag under the seat or above you, phone off, seat belt closed until the light is off.
We land at ten past two. Local time is one hour later than here.
If you have any questions, ask at the desk before the gate. After the gate there is nobody.

title: Sightseeing
intro: İki günlük gezi yazısı. Neyi ne zaman görmeli?
text:
Two days in this city, and everybody says: see the castle. We saw it. It is worth visiting, but not on Saturday — the queue for the ticket is longer than the tour.
My advice: go on Monday morning. The guide starts at ten and there are six people, not sixty.
How about taking a bus tour first? Two hours, and after that you know where everything is. The tower, the museum, the old bridge. Then you choose.
The exhibition in the museum was the best part of the trip. Photos from nineteen twenty: the same streets, the same houses, different people. Worth seeing even if you don't like museums.
And the tower? Two hundred steps. From the top you see the sea. I stayed there half an hour and said nothing. That does not happen often.
Let's go again in September. The castle is open until eight then.

title: Telling about a trip
intro: Üç günlük gezi. İlk gün ile ikinci gün arasında ne değişiyor?
text:
We arrived on Friday evening and the weather was terrible. Rain, wind, and the hotel was on the wrong side of the town. I said nothing for an hour.
Saturday was amazing. Sun from seven, the sea warm, and a boat trip for nine euros. Nine! At home a boat trip costs that much for ten minutes.
We stayed there for three days. On Sunday we made a picnic next to the water. Bread, cheese, tomatoes, and a wonderful view over the sea.
The people there work in the summer and read in the winter. A man in the shop told me that. He said it like a plan, not like a problem.
I want to go there again. Not in August — in June, when the water is cold and the town is quiet.
My friend asked: Would you like to go next year? I said: I'd love to.

title: A wedding
intro: Bahçede bir düğün. Kim ne yapıyor, kim ne diyor?
text:
I have been to three weddings this year, and the last one was the best.
The wedding was in a garden, not in a hall. Thirty guests, four tables, and a tree with roses on it.
The bride wore a long white dress and her mother cried before the first word. Her father did not cry. He photographed everything and said nothing for two hours.
My friend wore a blue suit and new shoes. After an hour the shoes came off. After two hours everybody took the shoes off and we danced on the grass.
At eleven the music stopped and the guests sat down. Then the bride's grandmother told a story about her wedding in 1962. Rain, twelve guests, and no photographs.
She said: The garden is nice. But the people are the wedding.

title: Close friends
intro: On yıllık bir arkadaşlık. Ne zaman yakın oldular?
text:
We have been friends for ten years. We met at school, in a corridor, both late for the same class.
At first we were not close. She was loud, I was quiet, and we shared nothing except the bus.
Then in the second year my father was ill for four months. She came every Friday with bread from her mother and sat with me. We did not talk about it. We watched films and laughed at bad jokes.
That is when I learned what friendship is. Not the big words — the Friday.
Now we live in two cities. We call every week and we see each other four times a year. It is enough.
Thank you for those Fridays, I said last year. She said: Thanks for opening the door.

title: Using a smartphone
intro: Üç sık soru, üç kısa cevap. Hangisi hangi sorunu çözüyor?
text:
Three things people ask me every week.
My phone is slow. First open Settings, then tap Update. Usually the phone is not slow — it is old inside. An update takes eight minutes and you get a new keyboard too.
Nothing works. Turn it off and turn it on again. I know how that sounds. It works because the phone forgets everything it did wrong since the morning.
The battery is empty at two in the afternoon. Look at Settings again. There is a list: which app took how much. The first one on that list is usually a map you opened in June.
And one more thing. The speaker gets quiet after two years. Clean it — thirty seconds, and it is loud again.
I don't think phones are hard. I think the menus are.

Question: My daughter is thirteen and wants an account. What do you say?

title: Useful apps
intro: Üç uygulama ve silinen bir tanesi. Hangisi neye yarıyor?
text:
Three apps I use every week, and one I deleted.
The first one is for finding a bus. I use this app to see when the next bus comes, not where it goes. Two seconds, no map, no account. Free.
The second is for words. I downloaded it to read the news in English and now I use it for everything. You press a word and the meaning comes. It costs nothing for the first month.
The third one is a list. Not a clever list — a stupid one. You write, you press, it is there. Every clever list app I installed was too slow to be useful.
And the one I deleted? A program for my photos. It was free, it was fast, and it wanted my address, my birthday and my phone number. For photos.
That is the question I ask now. Not what does it do — what does it want?

title: What I think about technology
intro: İyi mi kötü mü? Yazar soruyu değiştiriyor.
text:
Somebody asked me: is technology good or bad? I think that is the wrong question.
I think phones are useful. My mother is eighty-one and she sees her grandchildren every week on a screen. Twenty years ago she saw them twice a year.
But the same phone woke me at two in the morning last Tuesday for a message about a shop.
So: it depends on the app. It depends on the hour. It depends on who decides — you or the thing in your hand.
A colleague says technology is a waste of time. I agree with you about the games, I said, and then I asked: how did you find this restaurant? On the phone. And the train? On the phone.
The colleague laughed. That is my point, I said. The question is not good or bad. The question is who is holding whom.

Police: Good afternoon. What happened?

Ela: On the tram, line two, between the station and the market.
Police: When?
Ela: It happened at about six o'clock. I paid at the market at half past five and at six the wallet was gone.
Police: What was in it?
Ela: My ID card, a transport card, twenty euros and a photo.
Police: Can you describe the wallet?
Ela: Brown, small, with a broken button.
Police: And the tram was full?
Ela: Very full. Somebody stood very close for two stops.
Police: Then it is not lost. Somebody stole it. That is a different report.
Ela: Does that change something?
Police: For the insurance, yes. And for us: three today on line two.

title: At the library
intro: Kütüphane kuralları. Ne serbest, ne değil?
text:
Rules at the desk
You can borrow four books for three weeks. Members borrow eight. Membership is free for people under eighteen and for students.
You have to be quiet in the reading room. You can't eat here — water is fine, coffee is not. The machine downstairs is for that.
If you haven't returned a book after three weeks, you pay a fine of twenty euros at most. Somebody once paid twenty euros for a dictionary they lost in the kitchen at home.
You can take a notebook and a pen inside, but not a bag. The shelf at the entrance is free.
The silent room on the second floor is really silent. No talking, no calls, no keyboards. Twelve seats, and they are full by nine in the morning.
Renew online. Nobody wants to come here to say: three more weeks, please.

Dear Sir or Madam,
I would like to make a complaint about the rubbish in Garden Street.
They collect the rubbish on Mondays. In our street they have not come since the twelfth of August. That is three weeks. I have waited for three weeks and I have called twice.
The first time somebody said: we send a car on Thursday. No car came. The second time nobody answered.
I know the reason is not one person. But there is a list and our street is not on it.
Please put it on the list. I expect an answer within a week.
If you need a photo, I have eleven.
Yours faithfully,
Nil Aslan

intro: Şehrin takvimi. Ne zaman ne oluyor?
text:
What the city does and when
They collect the rubbish on Mondays and Thursdays. Paper is Monday only. You have to separate the paper from everything else — a bag with both is not collected and stays there until the next week.
They recycle glass at three points in this area: at the market, behind the school and next to the bakery. Glass is not collected from the houses.
Water and energy bills come four times a year. If you pay by card, they come by email. If you pay at the bank, they come on paper and two weeks later.
The tax office is open on Tuesday and Thursday until four, and on the first Saturday of the month until twelve. That Saturday is the quiet one — everybody comes on Tuesday.
One number for everything: it is on the trash can.

title: Writing a CV
intro: Yirmi saniyede karar veren üç şey. Hangisi neden önemli?
text:
Three things that decide a CV in twenty seconds.
Order. The reader starts at the top and stops when it gets boring. Put the last job first and the degree after it, not before. Nobody reads a CV from 2009 to today.
Time. Every job needs two dates and no gaps. If there is a gap, write one line: travelled, studied, cared for a parent. A gap with no line is a question; a gap with a line is a fact.
Proof. „Reliable and careful“ says nothing, because everybody writes it. „I had finished my degree before I started there, so I worked and studied for two years“ says the same thing and can be checked.
One more thing about the previous employer. Ask for the reference before you leave, not six months later. People change jobs, and the person who knows your work today may be somewhere else in April.
And the training courses: only the ones that touch this job. A CV is not a list of everything you have done. It is an answer to one question — why this person for this position?
Two pages at most. One is better.

Can: I read the advert. The number there works for me.
Deniz: You have to give one month's notice, yes?

Deniz: Then March. You don't have to wear a suit here, by the way. Nobody does.

One more thing, and it is not urgent. The old agenda template is still used by two teams. It was replaced in March. If you are one of those teams, nobody told you, and that is on us.

Deniz

Boss: That is a clear number. Why eight?

Boss: The middle is a fair place to start. The problem is the budget: it was written in October and it is not opened again until April.

Boss: If I get the department budget in April, I will do eight from January. If they say no, I can offer a bonus in July instead.
Ela: If they offered a bonus only, I would still want the raise written somewhere.
Boss: That is reasonable. I will put both in an email today, so neither of us remembers it differently in April.

title: The appraisal
intro: Bir değerlendirme görüşmesi. Zor olan kısım hangisiymiş?
text:
My appraisal was on a Tuesday at four, which is the worst hour for honest words.
She said that I had improved. Then she said the line I remember: the progress is real, but nobody outside this room can see it.
I asked what she meant. She told me to write down three things I had finished in the last six months, in one line each. Nine words, she said. Not nine pages.
I had thought criticism was the hard part of an appraisal. It is not. The hard part is praise you cannot use. „Good work“ goes nowhere. „You closed the thing that had been open for two years“ goes into the next conversation about salary.
She asked if I was happy. I said yes and then I said: not with the target. The target was written in January by somebody who had left in March.
We set a new one together. It is smaller and it has a date.
The last thing she told me was not about work. She said that most people leave an appraisal and do nothing for eleven months. Then they remember it the week before the next one.
I wrote the three lines that evening. It took twenty minutes and I have used them twice since.

title: Moving day
intro: Taşınma günü. Ne plana uydu, ne uymadı?
text:
The van came at nine, which is the only thing that went to plan.
I had packed everything except the kitchen. I am going to unpack the kitchen first, I said at eight, and I believed it. At four in the afternoon the kitchen was still four boxes in the corridor and I was looking for a knife.
Two men carried the cupboard upstairs and stopped. It did not go through the door. They took the doors off the cupboard, carried it in two parts, and put it back together in the bedroom. Twenty minutes. They had done it before.
The fragile box was the one I carried myself. Six glasses from my grandmother, one towel between each. I will carry that one, I said at every step, and nobody argued.
The meter reading is the thing everybody forgets. I took a photo of both meters at ten past nine, before the first box came in. Three weeks later the gas company sent a bill for the previous flat and the photo closed the question in one email.
The last thing that went wrong was the address. Two streets in this city have almost the same name. The van driver knew. I did not.

title: The noise problem
intro: Üst kattaki çamaşır makinesi. Sorun nasıl çözülüyor?
text:
The family above us moved in in March. By May I knew their washing machine better than mine.
Although I asked twice, the noise continued. The first time I went up and said it politely at the door. The second time I wrote a note, which was a mistake — a note is easy to ignore and nobody has to look at you.
The walls are thin. However, we can talk about it. That line came from the woman downstairs, who had lived in the building for nineteen years and had heard four families through the same wall.
Despite the noise, I stayed calm, and that turned out to be the whole method. The man upstairs was not disturbing anybody on purpose. He was working nights and doing the washing at eleven because that was the only hour he had.
We moved the washing to seven in the evening and I moved my own calls to the kitchen, which is on the far side. Nobody apologised and nobody had to.
The thing I learned is small and it is not about noise. A person who is asked at the door answers a person. A person who gets a note answers a piece of paper.

title: Why I signed up
intro: Kursa neden kaydolunmuş? Kısa cevap gerçek cevap değil.
text:
I enrolled to practise my English. That is the short answer and it is not the real one.
The real one is that I had been in this country for four years and I could do everything except the thing I wanted most: say something at the end of a meeting and have it land.
I enrolled in order to get a certificate, too. That was the line I used at work, because a course with a certificate is a budget line and a course for confidence is not. Both reasons were true. Only one of them could be said out loud.
I sit in front so that I can hear better, which everybody thinks is about the teacher. It is not. It is so that I cannot see how many people are behind me.
The aim I wrote on the first day was: speak for two minutes without stopping. In April I did it, badly, about trains. Nobody clapped and the teacher said one word: again. So I did it again.
When I finish this course, I will start the next one. Not because the certificate is worth anything by itself — because the room is.

title: Reason and result
intro: Dört sözcük, tek fikir. Hangisi cümleye başlayabiliyor?
text:
Four words for one idea, and they do not go in the same place.
I was late because the train stopped. „Because“ introduces the reason and it can also start the sentence: Because the train stopped, I was late. Both are correct; the second one is more formal.
The train stopped, so I was late. „So“ introduces the result and it cannot start a sentence. That is the difference and it is the mistake I see most often.
Since the train stopped, I was late. „Since“ works like „because“ but it usually comes first, and it carries a small extra meaning: we both already know this part.
Therefore is the formal one. The train was cancelled. Therefore, the meeting was moved. In an email it is right. At a table it sounds like a machine.
One way to check. If you can put the two parts in either order, you are using because or since. If the order is fixed, it is so.
And one more thing: since also means from that time. Since March I have worked here. The reader knows which one from the tense, not from the word.

title: In the news
intro: Üç haber, üç edilgen biçim. Hangisi bitti, hangisi sürüyor?
text:
Three short items from this week, and three different things happening to three verbs.
The report on the bridge was published last week. It is finished, it is on the website, and the figures in it are from March. That is a closed event and the language shows it.
A decision was announced by the council on Tuesday. Here the source is named, because a decision without a name behind it is not news. The council announced it; the sentence is turned over to put the decision first.
The case is being investigated. Nothing is finished. Nobody has said who did what. This form says one thing only: the work is happening now and there is no result yet.
A witness has claimed that the second lane was closed on Monday morning. Claimed, not said — the paper is telling you it has one voice for this and no official source.
So far the council has not answered our questions. That line appears in almost every report of this kind and it is the most honest one on the page.

title: What had happened
intro: Kötü bir sabah. Hangi olay hangisinden önce oldu?
text:
By the time I arrived, the shop had closed. That is the short version and it hides the interesting part.
I had left my keys at home. I realised it at the bus stop, which is eight minutes from the door and eleven minutes back, so I ran.
The bag was on the table where I had put it the night before. Brown leather, one broken handle, a label with my name on it from a course in March. I took it and ran again.
On the bus I suddenly realised the second problem: the bag was the wrong one. Same shape, same size, same material. My flatmate had bought hers in the same shop.
Luckily the man who found my bag on the bus the week before had left his number inside the front pocket. I called him from the shop door at two minutes past six, and he laughed before I finished the sentence.
He had had the same morning in April. His keys had been in the bag he did not take.
Finally I got home at seven. The mess on the table was the same mess. I put both bags in different rows on the shelf, and I wrote on one of them: not yours.

title: The place where I grew up
intro: Kıyıda küçük bir köy. İki virgül ne değiştiriyor?
text:
This is the village where I grew up. Four hundred people in winter, two thousand in August, and one road in between.
It is a place that tourists love for eleven days a year. They arrive in the last week of July, they photograph the same three houses on the hill, and by the middle of August the scenery is the only thing left.
The town, which is on the coast, is small. That comma matters. If I wrote „the town which is on the coast“, I would be choosing one town from several, and there is only one. The commas say: you already know which town, and here is something extra about it.
The valley behind the village is the peaceful part. Nobody photographs it because there is nothing in it: grass, a river, and the road to the next village where my grandmother was born.
The crowded weeks pay for the quiet ones. I understood that late, at about twenty-five, and my father said one sentence: we are not tired of them, we are tired in August.
I live in a city now and I go back twice a year. Never in August.

intro: Üye kuralları. Hangisi zorunlu, hangisi yasak, hangisi öğüt?
text:
For members, and for the people who bring them.
You must show your card at the door. Every time, also on the days when the person at the desk knows you. The rule is not about you; it is about the evening when somebody else is at the desk.
You mustn't bring food inside. Water in a bottle is fine. The reason is on the wall in one line: the room was repaired twice in four years and both times it was food.
You should ask for permission first if you want to bring a guest. Not must — should. Nobody has ever said no, but the room has twenty seats and the person who asks on Tuesday gets one.
Members who do not sign in are warned once. The second time there is a penalty of five euros, which goes into the coffee box and has paid for the coffee since March.
One more thing, and it is not a rule. If somebody behaves badly here twice in a row, three people will talk to them before anybody writes anything down. That has worked every time so far, and we would rather keep it that way.

title: This one or that one
intro: İki seçenek, iki bağlaç. Hangisi şaşırtıyor, hangisi karşılaştırıyor?
text:
Two machines, one table, and two sentences that look the same and are not.
Although it is cheaper, the quality is worse. That sentence has a surprise in it. Cheaper usually sounds good; the second half takes it away. „Although“ always works like that — it puts something you did not expect after something you did.
This one is small, whereas that one is big. No surprise anywhere. Two facts side by side, equal weight, and the reader is not being warned about anything. „Whereas“ compares; it does not concede.
The test is simple. Take the two halves and ask: does the second one take something back? If yes, you want „although“. If the two halves just stand next to each other, you want „whereas“.
In the end I preferred the first one, and not for the reason I expected. Both have the same quality. Both cost about the same. The difference was one button, which is on the front of one machine and behind the screen on the other.
I compare things for a living and I still decided on a button. That is worth knowing about myself.

title: The faulty order
intro: İkinci şikâyet mektubu. Hangi cümle tarihli, hangisi değil?
text:
Dear Sir or Madam,
I have written twice about this order and I am writing a third time, so I will keep it short.
I wrote to you on Monday the fourth and again on Thursday the seventh. The reference number is in both emails and at the top of this one.
The delivery arrived on the second. One of the two devices is faulty: it is switched on, the screen lights up for about a second, and then nothing. I have tried two plugs and two rooms.
I do not want a repair. The device was repaired once before it reached me — the box had been opened and closed with new tape, which I photographed before I opened it.
Could you replace it, please? I have the receipt, the reference number, and the photograph of the box.
I am not asking for an apology and I do not need goodwill. I need one working device, which is what I paid for on the last day of the month.
If a replacement is not possible, please say so in one line and I will ask for the money back instead.
Yours faithfully,
Ela Demir

title: The mix-up
intro: Yanlış kutu. Hangi olay hangisinden önce oldu?
text:
They had sent the wrong box. That is the end of the story and I am starting with it, because everything else is about when each person found out.
The box arrived on Tuesday. I opened it on Wednesday evening, after work, and I did not spot the mistake. The label was right. The number on the label was right. Everything inside was wrong.
Then I spotted the mistake, on Thursday morning, when I needed the small tool and found a large one. Two orders had been swapped in the warehouse on Monday, which means the wrong box had been on its way to me before I had even paid.
By the time I called, they had corrected it. Somebody in the warehouse had found the second box on Wednesday and had sent it on the same afternoon. Nobody told me, because the system sends one message per order and that message had already gone.
So the real confusion was not the box. It was four days in which two people were sorting the same problem and neither knew about the other.
I do not blame anybody for the swap. I blame the message that was sent once and could not be sent again.

title: Making up my mind
intro: İki seçenek tartılıyor. Aktarılan cümlelerde zaman nereye kayıyor?
text:
Two offers, one week, and four people who all wanted to help.
She said that it would be cheaper. That was the first opinion and it was correct: the second offer costs a hundred and twenty euros less a year. She had worked it out on paper before she said it, which is why I listened.
He told me to think about it again. Not because the number was wrong — because I had only considered the price. The disadvantage was in the second paragraph and I had read it twice without seeing it.
Then they asked if I had decided. That question came on Thursday and the honest answer was: I had decided three times and changed it twice.
So I did the boring thing. Two columns, advantages on the left, disadvantages on the right, and one rule: nothing goes in a column unless I can put a number next to it.
Four lines survived. Overall the first offer won by one line, and that line was not the price.
The conclusion I took away is not about offers. A choice with eleven reasons is a choice nobody has weighed. A choice with four is one you can explain to somebody else.

title: Registering here
intro: Kayıt işleminin dili. Cümleler neden hep edilgen?
text:
How registration works here, in the order it happens.
The form is stamped at the desk. Not by a person you can name — by whoever is there. That sentence has no time in it and that is the point: this is how it always works, on a Monday in March and on a Friday in August.
My application was processed last week. Here there is a time, so this is one event, mine, and it is over. Two sentences, same form, different jobs.
When is the card issued? Ten working days after the stamp, and the question is asked in the passive because nobody in the room issues it. It comes from another office in another building.
What you need: proof of address, the passport, and the old card if you have one. Residents who have lived here for less than three months bring the lease instead.
What nobody tells you: the desk is quiet between two and three, because the numbers are given out in the morning and most people come back after lunch.
And the part that is not in any guide: come in person on the first visit. Everything after that can be done by post, but the first stamp is given to a face.

title: Filling in the form
intro: Form doldurma kuralları. Hangisi zorunlu, hangisi değil?
text:
Six lines about a form that takes four minutes and is sent back twice a week.
You must fill in every section. An empty section is not read as „nothing to say“; it is read as „not finished“, and the form goes back in the post.
You should print your surname. Capital letters, one letter per box. The form is read by a scanner first and by a person second, and the scanner has no patience.
You don't have to give a phone number. That box has a small word next to it and the small word is „optional“. Three people in four fill it in anyway.
Tick one box in section four, not two. If both are true for you, tick the first and write the detail in section seven, which exists for exactly this.
The signature goes under the date, not next to it. This is the only line where the order matters, and it is the line most often wrong.
One last detail: use a black pen. Blue is accepted, but blue is copied badly and a bad copy is a second appointment.

intro: Üçüncü mektup. Resmî dil neyi değiştiriyor?
text:
Dear Ms Aslan,
Subject: account 4471 — request for a written reply
I am writing with a request about my account. The reference is in the subject line and on every page of this letter.
Although I wrote twice, I received no reply. The first letter was sent on the third of March and the second on the twenty-first. Both went to this address and neither came back.
The request itself is one sentence: I would like the annual statement for last year, on paper, with a stamp.
I have called four times. On each call I was told that the statement would be sent within ten working days, and on each call the ten days started again. I am not writing about the statement any more. I am writing because four people said the same thing and none of them wrote it down.
A copy of the first letter is attached, with the date on it.
If the statement cannot be issued, I would be grateful for one line saying so. A short no is better than a long silence.
I look forward to your reply at your earliest convenience.
Yours sincerely,
Deniz Kaya

title: What the policy covers
intro: Poliçenin üç cümlesi. Hangi koşul gerçek, hangisi değil?
text:
Three sentences from a policy and what each one really says.
If you have an accident, the policy covers it. Real condition, normal life: this can happen and here is what follows. Present in the first half, present in the second.
If I paid more, I would get a better policy. Not real. I am not paying more, and the sentence is about a policy that does not exist for me. The past form here is not about the past at all.
You are not covered unless you report it within seven days. This is the sentence that costs people money. „Unless“ means „if not“, and the seven days start on the day of the accident, not on the day you notice the damage.
The premium is the yearly payment. The benefit is what you get. Between them sits a number nobody reads: the first two hundred euros of any claim are yours.
So a small accident is not worth a claim. A big one is worth it twice, because the second thing insurance protects is your patience.
Read the „unless“ lines first. There are usually three and they are never in the same place.

title: Waiting my turn

segments.speaker: Nil
segments.text: The ticket said B62. The screen was showing B31, which sounds bad and is not: A, B and C move at different speeds.

segments.speaker: Nil
segments.text: Then they called my number. Two hours and ten minutes, which is under the average for a Monday.

title: Cinema on Saturday
intro: Deniz ile Emma'nın sinema planı yaptığı mesajlaşmayı okuyacaksın.
text:
Deniz: Hi Emma! What are you doing on Saturday?
Emma: Nothing special. I am at home. Why?
Deniz: There is a new film at the Star Cinema. It is a comedy.
Emma: Nice! What time does it start?
Deniz: At seven o'clock. But the tickets are cheap before six.
Emma: OK, can we meet early? I finish work at five.
Deniz: Sure. Let's meet at half past five in front of the cinema.
Emma: Perfect. Is Murat coming too?
Deniz: No, he is busy. He has got an exam on Monday.
Emma: Poor Murat! I have got twenty lira. Is that enough for a ticket?
Deniz: Yes, a ticket is fifteen lira. See you on Saturday!
Emma: See you!

LANGUAGE FRIENDS — Member Profile

Name: Elena Rossi
Age: 27
City: Milan, Italy
Job: nurse in a small hospital

About me:
Hello! I am Elena. I am 27 years old and I live in Milan with my sister. I work as a nurse. I start work at seven in the morning, so I am always tired at night!

I speak Italian and Spanish. Now I am learning English because I want to work in London. I have got a cat, and I love old films and long walks.

title: My Tuesday
intro: Bir öğrencinin salı gününü saat saat anlattığı günlük yazısını okuyacaksın.
text:
Tuesday, 14 March

I get up at half past six. I am always tired, but I open the window and drink a big glass of water.
At seven o'clock I have breakfast with my sister Elif. She makes tea.
I walk to school. It is twenty minutes.
Lessons start at eight. My favourite lesson is science, because our teacher is funny.
At half past twelve we have lunch. Today it is rice and a small salad.
After school I go to the library with Deniz. We do our homework there until five.
In the evening I help my mother in the kitchen. Then I watch a film.
I go to bed at eleven. Tomorrow is Wednesday and I have got a maths exam!

Greetings from Antalya! We arrived on Friday evening. The hotel is small but very nice. Our room has got a big balcony.

On Saturday we were at the beach all day. The water was warm and my brother swam for two hours. In the afternoon we ate fish at a small restaurant near the harbour. It cost only 200 lira!

On Sunday morning I visited the old town with Dad. We walked for three hours and I took forty photos. Mum stayed at the hotel because she was tired.

Now I am sitting on the balcony. The sun is going down and the sea is orange. I am writing this postcard to you.

See you next week!
Deniz

segments.text: Hi. I'd like a cheese sandwich and a small coffee, please.

segments.speaker: Waiter
segments.text: Sure. Do you want milk in your coffee?

segments.speaker: Emre
segments.text: No, thanks. I don't like milk. But I'd like some water too.

segments.speaker: Waiter
segments.text: Of course. That's seven dollars fifty.

segments.speaker: Emre
segments.text: Here you are. Is the sandwich hot?

segments.speaker: Waiter
segments.text: Yes, it is. It's coming in five minutes. What's your name?

segments.speaker: Emre
segments.text: Emre. E-M-R-E. Thanks.

segments.speaker: Waiter
segments.text: Thank you, Emre. Please take a seat by the window. Your order is coming.

questions.text: What does Emre order to eat?
questions.explain: Emre "I'd like a cheese sandwich and a small coffee, please." diyor; yani peynirli sandviç istiyor.

questions.text: How much is the order?
questions.explain: Garson fiyatı "That's seven dollars fifty." diye söylüyor.

questions.text: Emre wants milk in his coffee.
questions.explain: Garson "Do you want milk in your coffee?" diye soruyor, Emre "No, thanks. I don't like milk." diyor. Yani sütlü istemiyor.

questions.text: When is the sandwich ready?
questions.explain: Garson sandviç için "It's coming in five minutes." diyor.

questions.text: The order is ___ dollars fifty.
questions.explain: Garson "That's seven dollars fifty" diyor; sandviç ve kahve birlikte.

questions.text: Where does the waiter ask Emre to sit?
questions.explain: "Please take a seat by the window."

title: First Day at the Course
intro: Dil kursunun ilk gününde kendini sınıfa tanıtan bir öğrenciyi dinleyeceksin.

segments.speaker: Emre
segments.text: Hello, everyone. My name is Emre. I'm from Turkey. My city is Izmir. I'm twenty-four years old. I'm a nurse and I work at a big hospital.

segments.speaker: Emre
segments.text: I've got two brothers and one sister. Here in London I'm living with my aunt. I can speak a little English, but I can't speak French. I love music and football.

segments.speaker: Emre
segments.text: My class is on Monday and Wednesday at six o'clock. I'm going to study here for six months. I'm a little nervous today, but I'm very happy. Nice to meet you all.

questions.text: What is Emre's job?
questions.explain: Emre "I'm a nurse and I work at a big hospital" diyor, yani hemşire.

questions.text: How old is Emre?
questions.explain: "I'm twenty-four years old" cümlesinden yaşını anlıyoruz: 24.

questions.text: Emre can speak French.
questions.explain: Yanlış. "I can speak a little English, but I can't speak French" diyor; Fransızca bilmiyor.

questions.text: When is his class?
questions.explain: "My class is on Monday and Wednesday at six o'clock" diyor: pazartesi ve çarşamba.

questions.explain: "I'm going to study here for six months."

questions.text: Who is Emre living with in London?
questions.explain: "Here in London I'm living with my aunt." Kardeşleri Türkiye'de.

title: Where Is the Train Station?
intro: Sokakta bir turistin yol sorduğu konuşmayı dinleyeceksin.

segments.speaker: Emre
segments.text: Excuse me. I'm looking for the train station. Is it near here?

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: It's not very near, but you can walk. It's about ten minutes.

segments.speaker: Emre
segments.text: Okay. Which way is it?

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: Go straight on this street. Then turn left at the bank.

segments.speaker: Emre
segments.text: Turn left at the bank. And then?

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: Then take the second street on the right. It's called Green Street.

segments.speaker: Emre
segments.text: Is there a bus stop near the station?

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: Yes, there are two bus stops in front of it. You can't miss it.

segments.speaker: Emre
segments.text: Thank you very much!

questions.text: What is Emre looking for?
questions.explain: Emre ilk cümlede "I'm looking for the train station" diyor. Tren istasyonunu arıyor.

questions.text: How long is the walk?
questions.explain: Kadın "It's about ten minutes" diyor, yani yürüyüş yaklaşık on dakika.

questions.text: Emre must turn right at the bank.
questions.explain: Yanlış. Kadın "Then turn left at the bank" diyor; bankada sola dönmesi gerekiyor.

questions.text: How many bus stops are in front of the station?
questions.explain: Kadın "there are two bus stops in front of it" diyor, yani istasyonun önünde iki durak var.

questions.text: Turn left at the ___.
questions.explain: "Then turn left at the bank." Sağa değil, sola dönülüyor.

questions.text: What is the name of the second street on the right?
questions.explain: "Then take the second street on the right. It's called Green Street."

title: Green Market Announcement
intro: Bir süpermarkette hoparlörden yapılan indirim ve kapanış saati duyurusunu dinleyeceksin.

segments.speaker: Announcement
segments.text: Good afternoon, shoppers. Welcome to Green Market. It's three o'clock, and we've got some special offers for you today. Fresh apples are only two pounds a kilo.

segments.speaker: Announcement
segments.text: They're in aisle four, next to the bananas. We've got a big sale on bread too — buy two, get one free. That's in aisle six.

segments.speaker: Announcement
segments.text: Milk and cheese are in aisle one, at the back of the store. Don't forget, the store is closing at eight o'clock this evening. Please come to the checkout ten minutes before.

segments.speaker: Announcement
segments.text: Thank you for shopping with us. Have a nice day!

questions.text: Which aisle are the apples in?
questions.explain: Duyuruda "They're in aisle four, next to the bananas." deniyor, yani elmalar dördüncü reyonda.

questions.text: If you buy two loaves of bread, you get one free.
questions.explain: "We've got a big sale on bread too — buy two, get one free." cümlesi iki ekmek alana bir tanesinin bedava olduğunu söylüyor.

questions.text: How much are the fresh apples?
questions.explain: "Fresh apples are only two pounds a kilo." diyor, yani kilosu iki pound.

questions.text: What time is the store closing?
questions.explain: "the store is closing at eight o'clock this evening" cümlesi kapanış saatinin sekiz olduğunu söylüyor; saat üç ise duyurunun yapıldığı saat.

questions.text: The apples are in aisle ___.
questions.explain: "Fresh apples ... They're in aisle four, next to the bananas."

questions.text: Where are the milk and cheese?
accept: at the back of the store
